description: Verify that DUT correctly reassembles a 4-fragment Echo Request received OUT OF ORDER (frag 0, frag 2, frag 1, frag 3) and emits an Echo Reply with matching id/seq/data — fragments may arrive in any order (RFC 791 §3.2)
approach:
[Objective]
IP fragments can arrive at the receiver in any order — middlebox queueing, multipath routing, retransmission. Reassembly must use offset to place each fragment, not arrival order. This case sends 4 fragments deliberately out of order and confirms the result is correct.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: fragment 0 (offset=0, MF=1)
2. Tester → DUT: fragment 2 (offset=2X, MF=1)
3. Tester → DUT: fragment 1 (offset=X, MF=1)
4. Tester → DUT: fragment 3 (offset=3X, MF=0)
   ⇒ DUT must reassemble using offset positions, regardless of arrival order.

5. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: Echo Reply with full payload, id, seq matching the original Request.

[Pass condition]
Reply id, seq, and data all match.

[Fail condition]
Same as IPV4_FRAGMENTS_01 — Fail_echo_id / Fail_echo_seq / Fail_data_mismatch / Fail_timeout.

verdicts.Pass: DUT reassembled out-of-order fragments correctly — normal
verdicts.Fail_data_mismatch: Reply data did not match expected payload — reassembly used arrival order
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit a Reply within the window
